edges.label: DERIVED-UNDER-ASSUMPTION
assumptions: Stellar mass limits scale as in the cited papers: minimum mass set by electron degeneracy versus nuclear ignition, maximum mass set by radiation pressure, both in units of the Chandrasekhar mass; the ratio depends on the constants only through beta/alpha^2.
Gravity (G), the proton mass and the nuclear burning physics are held fixed; only alpha and beta change.
The thresholds 1/464, 1/200 and 1/100 are imported as published (Adams 2019, Tegmark 1998, Barnes 2012); their spread is reported as CONTESTED, not averaged.
edges.notes: PASS beta/alpha^2 >= 1/100 (above all three published limits: 1/464 Adams 2019, 1/200 Tegmark 1998, 1/100 Barnes 2012). CONTESTED between 10^(-8/3) ~ 1/464 and 1/100. FAIL below 10^(-8/3): the smallest hydrogen-burning star would outweigh the largest stable one. The scaling with beta/alpha^2 is derived (derive.d6); the three thresholds are imported from the cited papers. At our beta: alpha must stay below 0.233 (Barnes), 0.330 (Tegmark) or 0.503 (Adams). SOURCE CHECK (2026-11-16, papers re-read): the single-combination form beta >~ 10^(-8/3) alpha^2 is Adams 2019 eq. (23), p.26 (from eqs. A.4-A.5): VERIFIED. Adams 2008 (eqs. 41-45) does not reduce the mass-window closure to beta/alpha^2 alone (it depends on kT_nuc/m_e c^2, with T_nuc from eq. 42 involving G, C and m_e^3 kappa0), so the beta/alpha^2 scaling is Adams 2019's simplified form, not a result of Adams 2008. At our beta the FAIL edge (alpha = 0.503 = 69 alpha0) is consistent with Adams 2008 Fig. 5 (about 10^2 alpha0 at G0, read by eye).

edges.label: DERIVED-UNDER-ASSUMPTION
assumptions: Earliest galaxies at redshift z ~ 4, as used by Martel, Shapiro & Weinberg 1998.
Primordial fluctuation amplitude Q and dark-matter-to-photon ratio held at our values (Tegmark et al. 2006 show the bound scales with Q^3).
Our density ratio Omega_Lambda/Omega_m = 0.685/0.315 (Planck 2018).

Spherical top-hat collapse with the linear growing mode (MSW 1998 eq. 4 and eq. 57); collapse at z = 4 means linear overdensity 1.686 (Einstein-de Sitter value, IMPORTED); Lambda negligible before z = 4.

Applies to positive Lambda. For negative Lambda, structure forms readily in the recollapsing phase (Peacock 2007), so this link PASSes; the negative-Lambda limit is the lifetime link l.s11.lambda-lifetime.
edges.notes: Weinberg 1987 and MSW 1998 eq. (4), p.6: a spherical fluctuation recollapses iff rho_V <= (500/729) delta^3 rhobar, with delta the linear growing-mode overdensity at recombination (MSW use the growing-mode sigma, eq. 57). A galaxy at z ~ 4 has linear overdensity 1.686 at z = 4, and delta^3 rhobar is invariant under linear growth, so rho_V <= (500/729) 1.686^3 (1+z)^3 rho_m0 = 411 rho_m0. With Omega_m = 0.315 (Planck 2018) and Omega_Lambda = 0.685, rho_Lambda,ours = 2.17 rho_m0, so the bound is 189 in dial units. Until atlas@locked-2026-11-16a this link used 57.5 = 125/2.17, treating (1+z)^3 rho_m0 = 125 rho_m0 as the bound; MSW p.3 and Weinberg 1996 p.3 state 125 rho_m0 only as a value the bound cannot be much less than (docs/locks/LOCKED_LAMBDA_GALAXY_189.md). MSW also find the observed-typical value is much smaller than this bound. FAIL above the bound; PASS below.

edges.to_name: Hydrogen and a periodic table with C and O
edges.label: IMPORTED
edges.notes: Carbon and heavier nuclei hold together iff alpha_s >= 0.3*sqrt(alpha), with alpha_s = 0.1 scaled by the strong dial (Tegmark 1998, citing Barrow & Tipler). | CONTESTED NUCLEAR EDGES (Chemist lock C2, informational, do not change this link's condition): (a) deuteron unbinds at s in [-0.06, -0.04]; (b) diproton binds at s in [+0.06, +0.17]. Ranges are model-dependent: square well -4%/+6%, Yukawa -6%/+17% (Adams, Phys. Rep. 807 (2019), arXiv:1902.03928, sec. 2.4, last paragraph, arXiv PDF p. 31, citing Davies, J. Phys. A 5 (1972) 1296). ASSUMED: nuclear well depth scales linearly with alpha_s, so s = fractional change in alpha_s (as in MacDonald & Mullan 2009, V = G^2 V0, s = G^2 - 1; their diproton binding at G = 1.065 gives s = 0.134, inside (b)). Neither edge fails a universe. Dissent on (a): Adams & Grohs, Astropart. Phys. 91 (2017) 90-104, doi:10.1016/j.astropartphys.2017.03.009 (stars without stable deuterium). Dissent on (b): MacDonald & Mullan, PRD 80, 043507 (2009), arXiv:0904.1807 (primordial H survives for G < 1.5). Stage version kept on branch chemist-c2-stages for a later PR. PRE-EMPTED (slate A1, 2026-11-16): this link FAILs only for alpha > 0.071, where l.s05.hydrogen-stable already FAILs (it FAILs for every alpha > 0.0244 at any beta in range), so it never decides a verdict alone in the current dial ranges.

edges.to_name: Hydrogen and a periodic table with C and O
edges.label: DERIVED-UNDER-ASSUMPTION
assumptions: The electromagnetic part of the neutron-proton mass difference scales linearly with alpha (leading order).
Quark masses (and so the QCD part Q) are held fixed while alpha changes.
Errors on Q and E are treated as independent 1-sigma intervals.
edges.notes: m_n - m_p = Q + E*(alpha/alpha0), Q = 2.52 +/- 0.29 MeV (QCD), E = -1.00 +/- 0.16 MeV (QED) (Borsanyi et al. 2015). Hydrogen is stable against electron capture iff m_n - m_p > m_e = beta * 938.272 MeV. PASS if stable over the whole 1-sigma box, FAIL if unstable over all of it, else CONTESTED. At beta = ours the central critical alpha is 2.01 x ours (0.01466); band 1.48-2.73 x ours.

edges.to_name: Hydrogen and a periodic table with C and O
edges.label: DERIVED-UNDER-ASSUMPTION
assumptions: The Coulomb coefficient a_c scales linearly with alpha and the surface coefficient a_s scales linearly with the strong-force change s; all other nuclear structure is held fixed.
Liquid-drop coefficients a_s = 17.8 MeV, a_c = 0.711 MeV (one published fit; other fits differ by a few percent).
Nuclei follow the valley-of-stability relation Z = A/2 - 0.2 A^2/(A + 200) (approximation used in derive.py, not separately sourced).

The table ends where spontaneous fission becomes barrier-free (Z^2/A at the Bohr-Wheeler limit) or where the 1s level dives into the Dirac sea (Z ~ 1.24/alpha); shell effects and islands of stability are ignored.
Electron masses and the proton mass are held fixed.
edges.notes: Periodic table ends at min(relativistic limit Z ~ 1.24/alpha (Z_cr ~ 170 at our alpha, Zeldovich & Popov 1972), liquid-drop fission limit Z^2/A = 2*a_s*(1+s)/(a_c*alpha/alpha0) (Bohr & Wheeler 1939), with a_s = 17.8 MeV and a_c = 0.711 MeV (Rohlf 1994 fit)). PASS end >= 26 (iron); WEAK 8 <= end < 26 (C and O exist, heavier missing); FAIL end < 8. Z_fission(alpha, strong) = largest Z with Z^2/A(Z) below that limit, A(Z) from the valley-of-stability approximation in derive.py. Ours: relativistic 137 (Dirac) to 169 (finite nucleus), fission 134. PRE-EMPTED (slate A1, 2026-11-16): FAIL (L < 8) needs alpha > 0.075, where l.s05.hydrogen-stable already FAILs, so it never decides a verdict alone in the current dial ranges.

edges.label: CONTESTED
assumptions: Spatially flat universe dominated by matter after early times; radiation ignored. The lifetime then depends only on |Lambda|.
Observers need at least as long as they took here (13.787 Gyr, Planck 2018). This is a one-sample benchmark, not a derived requirement.
The heating-to-8 K cutoff that Peacock 2007 discusses is not modelled.
edges.notes: Negative Lambda makes a flat universe recollapse. Its total lifetime is t = (2*pi/3)/H_L with H_L = sqrt(8*pi*G*|rho_Lambda|/3), exact for flat matter + Lambda < 0 (derive.d11). With Planck 2018 H0 = 67.4 km/s/Mpc and Omega_Lambda = 0.685, t = 36.7 Gyr / sqrt(|x|) for dial value x < 0. The anthropic condition for negative Lambda is that the universe survives long enough for observers (Barrow & Tipler 1986, as stated by Martel, Shapiro & Weinberg 1998). The literature gives no agreed lifetime threshold: Peacock 2007 finds that structure forms readily while recollapsing, and that negative Lambda is disfavoured only if observers cannot form once the recollapsing universe heats above 8 K. The condition shown uses our own single sample as the benchmark (observers at 13.787 Gyr, Planck 2018), giving x >= -7.09. With a 5 Gyr benchmark it would be x >= -53.9. CONTESTED because the threshold is an assumption, not a result. PASS for every positive Lambda.
